# Compile-time optimization options are exposed through -ldflags.
! go build -o2 .
stderr 'flag provided but not defined: -o2'
! go build -o3 .
stderr 'flag provided but not defined: -o3'
! go build -ldflags=-o3=invalid .
stderr 'invalid boolean value "invalid"'
! go build -ldflags=-fmth=invalid .
stderr 'invalid boolean value "invalid"'

# By default, only command-line packages are affected.
go build -a -n '-ldflags=-o2 -fmth' .
stderr 'compile.* -p main .* -o2 -fmth '
! stderr 'compile.* -p example.com/flags/dep .* -fmth '

# O3 follows the same package matching and compiler-override rules as O2.
go build -a -n '-ldflags=all=-o3' '-gcflags=example.com/flags/dep=-o3=false' .
stderr 'compile.* -p main .* -o3 '
stderr 'compile.* -p example.com/flags/dep .* -o3 -o3=false '

# Patterns cover dependencies and later matching flags take precedence.
go build -a -n '-ldflags=all=-o2 -fmth' '-ldflags=example.com/flags/dep=-fmth=false' .
stderr 'compile.* -p main .* -o2 -fmth '
stderr 'compile.* -p example.com/flags/dep .* -fmth=false '
! stderr 'compile.* -p example.com/flags/dep .* -o2 '

# Explicit compiler flags can override the linker-facing defaults.
go build -a -n '-ldflags=-fmth' '-gcflags=-fmth=false' .
stderr 'compile.* -p main .* -fmth -fmth=false '

# Toggling the flags also invalidates dependency compilation caches and works
# through go test's generated test packages.
env FMTH=false
go test ./dep
env FMTH=true
go test -ldflags=-fmth ./dep
env FMTH=false
go test -ldflags=-fmth=false ./dep

-- go.mod --
module example.com/flags

go 1.28
-- main.go --
package main
import "example.com/flags/dep"
func main() { println(dep.F(2)) }
-- dep/dep.go --
package dep
//go:noinline
func F(x float64) float64 { return x / x }
-- dep/dep_test.go --
package dep_test
import (
	"example.com/flags/dep"
	"os"
	"testing"
)
func TestOptimization(t *testing.T) {
	if got, want := dep.F(0) == 1, os.Getenv("FMTH") == "true"; got != want {
		t.Fatalf("optimized = %v; want %v", got, want)
	}
}
